item.title: ASP.NET MVC File Upload Implementation Techniques and Byte Array Conversion
item.description:
“ASP.NET MVC File Upload Implementation Techniques and Byte Array Conversion”

When dealing with file uploads in an ASP.NET MVC application, developers often face the challenge of correctly binding the file input and processing the uploaded data on the server side. Furthermore, the requirement to persist this data—either as a file on the server or as binary data within a database—necessitates specific coding patterns.

What are the established patterns for processing file uploads using HttpPostedFileBase in ASP.NET MVC controllers, and how can the resulting file stream be effectively converted into a byte array for storage or other operations?

item.title: Solved: How to Perform Asynchronous File Uploads with JavaScript and jQuery
item.description:
“Solved: How to Perform Asynchronous File Uploads with JavaScript and jQuery”

Solutions

Method 1: Utilizing HTML5 FormData with jQuery $.ajax() for Modern Browsers

The most widely accepted and efficient method for asynchronous file uploads leverages HTML5’s FormData API combined with jQuery’s powerful $.ajax() function. This approach allows for file validation, progress tracking, and sending additional form data.

HTML Structure for File Input

Begin with a simple HTML form containing a file input and an upload button. A <progress> element is also helpful for displaying upload status.

item.title: Solved: How to Upload Files Using Django Rest Framework
item.description:
File uploading in Django Rest Framework (DRF) is a common requirement but comes with its challenges. This guide provides answers to the most pressing questions and offers practical, step-by-step solutions tailored to developers using Django and AngularJS.

Key Questions Addressed

  1. How can you verify if request.FILES contains data in Django Rest Framework?
  2. What is the best approach to serialize file fields?
  3. When and how should you use parsers like MultiPartParser in DRF?

Solution 1: Using pre_save Hook (Deprecated)

Although pre_save is now deprecated in DRF 3.0+, understanding its usage is insightful for legacy projects.
